$$b\cdot\nu_a+d_a\ge0\qquad(a\in A)$$

if and only if every $\lambda\in\mathbb R^A$ with $\lambda_a\ge0$ and $\sum_{a\in A}\lambda_a\nu_a=0$ satisfies $\sum_{a\in A}\lambda_ad_a\ge0$. If an actual transition has entropy change $\Delta\sigma_a\ge d_a$, such a vector guarantees $\Delta\sigma_a+b\cdot\nu_a\ge0$. The criterion is exact for the finite lower-bound inequalities; it does not claim necessity for actual transitions when $d_a$ is only a loose bound.

case_scope.source_excerpt:
Adopt the quantum Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for a finite list of independent modes at $T>0$. For a bosonic mode with excitation energy $\varepsilon>0$ joules, let $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$, and let $N$ be its dimensionless occupation number. Its partition trace and mean occupation are
$$Z_B=(1-q)^{-1},\qquad \langle N\rangle_B=\frac{q}{1-q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}.$$
For a fermionic two-level occupation system with energies $0,\varepsilon$, the partition sum and excited-state occupation are
$$Z_F=1+q,\qquad \langle N\rangle_F=\frac{q}{1+q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}.$$
For a finite independent collection, the corresponding partition traces multiply and each mode's marginal mean is the displayed one. These are exact model identities under the adopted preparation.

A finite positional configuration of $N$ classical point particles in $\Lambda$ is an unordered simple set $\omega=\{x_1,\ldots,x_N\}\subset\Lambda$; simple means that no point is repeated. A pair potential is an even measurable function $\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, where $\varphi(x)$ is the interaction energy in joules at physical displacement $\ell_0x$ and evenness means $\varphi(x)=\varphi(-x)$.
